● TRAI was established on 20th February 1997 by the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India Act, 1997.

Further Insight:

● Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI)

○ Formed on: February 20, 1997

○ Established under: Telecom Regulatory Authority of India Act, 1997

○ Primary Functions:

■ Regulating telecom services to ensure quality, transparency, and fair competition.

■ Protecting consumer interests by addressing grievances and promoting affordability.

■ Monitoring tariffs and ensuring reasonable pricing of telecom services.

■ Promoting innovation in telecom infrastructure and services.

○ TRAI plays a crucial role in shaping Indias telecom landscape and maintaining a balance between service providers and consumers.

● NITI Aayog replaces Planning Commission of India

Further Insight:

● The National Institution for Transforming India (NITI Aayog)

○ It is a policy think tank of the Government of India

○ Established on January 1,2015 to replace the Planning Commission.

○ Structure

■ NITI Aayog has a Governing Council chaired by the Prime Minister and Chief Ministers of all states and Lt. Governors of Union Territories.

■ The Prime Minister also appoints the Vice-Chairperson, Chief Executive Officer, and ex-officio members.

○ NITI Aayog's objectives are based on seven pillars of effective governance: pro-people, pro-activity, participation, empowerment, inclusion of everyone, equality, and transparency

○ NITI Aayog's mandate is to oversee the adoption and monitoring of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) in the country.

● Article 280 of the Indian constitution states that The President constitutes the Finances Commission every Fifth year.

Further Insight:

● Finance Commission of India

○ The Finance Commission is established under Article 280 of the Indian Constitution.

○ It is constituted by the President of India.

○ The first Finance Commission was formed in 1951.

○ The first chairman of the Finance Commission was K.C. Neogy.

○ The current chairman of the Finance Commission is Arvind Panagariya.

○ Major Objectives:

■ To recommend the distribution of taxes between the Centre and the States, and among the States themselves.

■ To determine the principles governing grants-in-aid to the States by the Centre.

■ To suggest measures to augment the Consolidated Fund of a State to supplement the resources of Panchayats and Municipalities.

■ To address both vertical and horizontal fiscal imbalances.

• The Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG) is the constitutional body that audits the government's finances to ensure transparency and accountability.

Further Insight:

Article 149Duties and Powers of the CAGDefines the duties and powers of the CAG in relation to auditing the accounts of the Union and State governments.
Article 150Uniformity in AccountsProvides for the establishment of a uniform form of accounts for the Union and States to maintain consistency.

questions.question: UPSC got its constitutional status on ____________. यूपीएससी को संवैधानिक दर्जा ____________ को मिला।
questions.solution:
• UPSC got constitutional status on January 26, 1950.

• Evolution of UPSC

○ The Royal Commission on Superior Civil Services in India (1923) recommended the creation of a Public Service Commission in its 1924 report.

○ First Public Service Commission established in 1926 with Sir Ross Barker as Chairman, having a limited advisory role.

○ Federal Public Service Commission created under the Government of India Act, 1935.

○ After India gained independence in 1947, the Federal Public Service Commission was renamed the Union Public Service Commission.

○ On January 26, 1950, the Constitution of India granted the UPSC constitutional status.

Further Insight:

• Union Public Service Commission (UPSC)

○ Founded on October 1, 1926.

○ Gained constitutional status on January 26, 1950.

○ Governed by Articles 315 - 323 of the Indian Constitution.

○ Article 315 mentions the Public Service Commission for the Union and for the States

○ Composition and Appointment:

■ Comprises a Chairman and ten members.

■ Members are appointed by the President of India.

■ Serve a term of six years or until the age of 65.

■ At least half the members have prior government experience

○ Conducts exams and recruits candidates for civil services and other government posts.

○ Plays a crucial role in ensuring qualified personnel for India's governance.

• Term of the Member or Chairman of State Service Commission or Joint Service commission is 6 years or 62 years of age whichever is earlier.

Further Insight:

• State Public Service Commission (SPSC)

○ Governed by Articles 315 - 323 of the Indian Constitution.

○ Article 315 mentions the Public Service Commission for the Union and for the States

○ Responsible for state-level recruitment and personnel management.

○ Composition and Appointment:

■ Comprises a Chairman and members appointed by the Governor.

■ At least half the members must have 10 years of government experience.

■ Members serve a 6-year term or until the age of 62.

○ Members can only be removed by the President of India.

■ Grounds for removal include insolvency or misconduct.

■ Requires consultation with the Supreme Court, if necessary.

○ Ensures independence with protected tenure.

○ Salaries are drawn from the state's Consolidated Fund, ensuring financial security.

• The procedure of removal of Chief Election Commissioner of India is the same as of Judges of the Supreme Court.

Further Insight:

• Articles Related to Elections and the Election Commission

○ Article 324:

■ Establishes the Election Commission of India (ECI) to oversee and ensure free and fair elections in the country. It grants the President the authority to appoint the Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners.

○ Article 325:

■ Provides for the creation of a common electoral roll for elections to the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies, ensuring that all citizens who are eligible can vote.

○ Article 326:

■ States that elections to the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies will be based on adult suffrage, meaning all citizens above the age of 18 are eligible to vote.

○ Article 327:

■ Empowers Parliament to make provisions for the conduct of elections to the Lok Sabha and to the State Legislatures.

○ Article 328:

■ Allows the State Legislatures to make provisions for the conduct of elections to the Legislative Assemblies of the states and to the offices of Chairpersons of Panchayats at different levels.

○ Article 329:

■ Prohibits the interference of courts in electoral matters, ensuring that the validity of elections is not questioned in a court of law.

○ Article 330:

■ Provides for the reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes (SCs) and Scheduled Tribes (STs) in the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies.

○ Article 331:

■ Empowers the President to nominate representatives of the Anglo-Indian community to the Lok Sabha if he/she believes that the community is not adequately represented.

○ Article 332:

■ Allows the reservation of seats for SCs and STs in the Legislative Assemblies of the states.

○ Article 333:

■ Empowers the Governor of a state to nominate not more than two members of the Anglo-Indian community to the Legislative Assembly if he/she feels that the community is not adequately represented.

■ It abolished

○ Article 334:

■ Relates to the reservation of seats for SCs and STs, and the Anglo-Indian community, and provides for their continuation for a period of ten years from the commencement of the Constitution, which has been extended multiple times.

• National Commission of Scheduled Tribes established under Article 338A by 89th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003.

Further Insight:

• National Commission for Scheduled Tribes (NCST)

○ Formed under Article 338-A through the 89th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003.

○ Became an independent body in 2004 to focus on Scheduled Tribes' welfare.

○ Investigates the implementation of legal safeguards for Scheduled Tribes (STs).

○ Addresses complaints regarding the rights and welfare of STs.

○ Advises governments on policies and socio-economic planning for STs.

○ Monitors and evaluates the progress of development programs for STs.

○ Secures forest rights and protects traditional tribal resources.

○ Addresses issues related to land rights and resource exploitation affecting STs.

• Article 350B was added by 7th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1956 for establishment of the office of Special officer for Linguistic Minorities

Further Insight:

• Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities

○ Established under Article 350-B, introduced by the Seventh Constitutional Amendment Act, 1956.

○ Mandates the President to appoint a Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities.

○ Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities

■ Created in 1957 to oversee linguistic minority rights.

■ Operates under the Ministry of Minority Affairs.

○ Headquarter located in Allahabad (Prayagraj).

○ Regional Offices: Functioning in Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, and West Bengal.

○ Function

■ Investigates and reports on the implementation of safeguards for linguistic minorities.

■ Ensures compliance with constitutional and legal protections for linguistic rights.

• Office of the Attorney General of India is mentioned under Article 76.

Further Insight:

• Attorney General of India

○ The Attorney General acts as the chief legal advisor to the government mentioned under Article 76.

○ They do not have a fixed term, and can be removed by the President any time.

○ He/She generally does not represent private parties in legal matters unless permitted by the Government of India.

○ He has the right to an audience in all courts in the territory of India.

○ He can sit in both houses and take part in debate but cannot vote in any resolution.

• Reserve Bank of India an autonomous body under Government of India is the regulator and supervisor of the financial system of India.

Further Insight:

• Reserve Bank of India (RBI) - Key Points

○ Established on April 1, 1935, under the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.

○ Originally located in Calcutta, the Central Office moved to Mumbai in 1937.

○ Nationalized in 1949, now fully government-owned.

○ Preamble: Focuses on monetary stability, a modern monetary policy framework, and price stability aligned with economic growth.

○ Structure: Governed by a central board appointed by the Government of India.

■ Directors: Governor, four Deputy Governors, ten nominated members, two government officials, and four regional board representatives.

○ Main Functions:

■ Monetary Authority: Implements monetary policy, with the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) established in 2016 to set inflation targets (currently 4% ±2%).

■ Financial Regulator: Oversees banking operations, issuing licenses, and setting parameters for the banking system.

■ Foreign Exchange Manager: Manages reserves, facilitates trade, and maintains rupee value.

■ Currency Issuer: Manages currency issuance and circulation.

■ Developmental Role: Supports rural finance and priority sector lending.

■ Financial Inclusion: Initiatives like No Frills Accounts and technology-based banking for wider access.

■ Banker to Government and Banks: Manages government funds, provides financial support to banks

questions.question: SEBI was established in the year ______. सेबी की स्थापना वर्ष ______ में हुई थी।

• SEBI or Securities and Exchange Board of India established on 12th April 1992 under the SEBI Act, 1992

Further Insight:

• Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)

○ Formed on: April 12, 1988

○ Established under: SEBI Act, 1992

○ Primary Functions:

■ Regulating the securities market to protect the interests of investors.

■ Promoting the development of the securities market by ensuring efficient functioning.

■ Preventing malpractices like insider trading, fraud, and unfair practices.

■ Regulating stock exchanges, brokers, and sub-brokers in the securities market.

• Function and role of NHRC

○ Act as a civil court for judicial proceeding and can investigate human rights violation

○ Authority to utilize central or state government officers and agencies for investigation of violation of human rights

Further Insight:

• National Human Rights Commission (NHRC)

○ Formed on 12th October 1993 under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993.

■ Amended in 2006 and 2019.

○ Its purpose is to Protects rights related to life, liberty, equality, and dignity as guaranteed by:

■ The Indian Constitution.

■ International covenants.

■ Investigates human rights violations within one year of their occurrence.

questions.question: When was the National commission for women established? राष्ट्रीय महिला आयोग की स्थापना कब की गई?

• National Commission for women established in 1992 under the National Commission for Women Act, 1990.

Further Insight:

• National Commission for Women (NCW)

○ National Commission for women established in 1992 under the National Commission for Women Act, 1990.

○ Its purpose is to advocate for women's rights and provide policy advice to the government on matters affecting women.

○ It focuses on

■ Dowry issues.

■ Gender equality in employment.

■ Prevention of exploitation and addressing rights violations.

○ Its main functions are

■ Investigates complaints related to:

• Violence against women.

• Discrimination.

• Violations of women's rights.

• NGT or National Green Tribunal handles the following dispute in India related to

○ Environmental Protection

○ Forest Protection

○ Natural Resource Management

Further Insight:

• National Green Tribunal (NGT)

○ Formed under the National Green Tribunal Act, 2010.

○ It's purpose is to Ensures swift and effective resolution of cases related to:

■ Environmental protection.

■ Forest conservation.

■ Natural resource management.

○ Handles disputes under seven key laws listed in Schedule I of the Act, including:

■ The Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974.

■ The Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980.

■ The Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981.

■ Others concerning environmental safeguards.

○ Aims to resolve cases within six months of filing.

• CVC or Central Vigilance Commission is the apex vigilance institution in India.

Further Insight:

• Central Vigilance Commission (CVC)

○ Apex vigilance institution in India.

○ Functions independently of any executive authority.

○ Set up in 1964 based on the recommendations of the Santhanam Committee.

■ Granted statutory status by the CVC Act, 2003.

○ Responsible for overseeing vigilance activities across all Central Government organizations.

■ Advises authorities in planning, implementing, reviewing, and reforming vigilance measures.

○ Structure

■ A Central Vigilance Commissioner (Chairperson).

■ Two Vigilance Commissioners.

○ Appointment

■ Appointed by the President based on recommendations of a three-member committee consisting of:

• The Prime Minister (Chairperson).

• The union Home minister.

• The Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha.

○ Functions:

■ Preventive Vigilance: Advises on systemic improvements to prevent corruption.

■ Supervisory Role: Monitors vigilance activities and complaints referred to the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI).

• Exercises superintendence over vigilance cases investigated by the CBI.

■ Inquiry Oversight: Directs inquiries into corruption cases within Central Government departments.

■ Coordination: Coordinates efforts to strengthen integrity in governance.

■ Training & Awareness: Promotes vigilance awareness and organizes training for officials.

• The Competition Commission of India or CCI is the government body who is responsible to prevent anti-competitive practices in the India market and promotes & sustains competition in the Indian market.

Further Insight:

• Competition Commission of India (CCI)

○ A statutory body established to implement and enforce the Competition Act, 2002.

■ Constituted in March 2009.

○ Mandate and Function

■ Promotes and sustains fair competition in the market.

■ Prevents practices that have an adverse effect on competition in India.

■ Protects the interests of consumers and ensures freedom of trade.

■ Prohibiting Anti-Competitive Agreements.

■ Regulates enterprises to prevent the misuse of their dominant position in the market.

■ Reviews mergers, acquisitions, and amalgamations to prevent combinations that may cause a significant adverse effect on competition within India.

○ Powers

■ Investigates anti-competitive practices through Director General (Investigation).

■ Can impose penalties and corrective measures for violations of the Competition Act.

■ Issues orders to modify or block mergers and acquisitions that harm competition.

• National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development or NABARD is a regulatory and statutory body responsible to regulate or supervise Regional Rural Banks.

Further Insight:

• National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD)

• Formed On: 1982

• Law Under Which It Was Formed: NABARD Act, 1981

• Primary Functions:

■ NABARD is a developmental financial institution focused on agriculture and rural development.

■ Its primary role is to provide credit and financial support for agricultural and rural development activities, particularly in the farming sector and small-scale industries.

■ NABARD also monitors and coordinates rural development policies and provides assistance to regional rural banks, cooperatives, and other financial institutions that lend to the rural economy.

■ It plays a crucial role in promoting sustainable agriculture, improving rural livelihoods, and supporting initiatives like irrigation, farm mechanization, and rural infrastructure development

• National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA)

○ Established in 1997 as an attached office of the Department of Pharmaceuticals.

○ Ensures fair and affordable pricing of drugs and medical devices in India.

○ Functions

■ Enforcement of Price Control:

• Implements and enforces the Drugs Price Control Order (DPCO), 1995/2013, under delegated powers.

■ Drug Pricing Studies:

• Conducts and sponsors studies on drug pricing and formulations to ensure transparency and affordability.

■ Monitoring Drug Availability:

• Monitors the availability of drugs, identifies shortages, and takes necessary corrective measures.

○ Collects and maintains data on:

■ Production and availability of bulk drugs and formulations.

■ Exports and imports.

■ Market shares and profitability of pharmaceutical companies.

○ Advises and assists the Central Government on drug policy revisions.

○ Provides support for parliamentary matters concerning drug pricing.
